item.title: Tesla Cybercab riders can now see behind the car on a live camera feed, days before Tesla's NHTSA deadline
item.description: Passengers in Austin's Cybercabs can now open the rear and side cameras during a ride, and a dark-screen quiet mode has appeared too. The update lands just ahead of Tesla's October 30 deadline to answer NHTSA's questions on mirrors and rear-view cameras.

item.title: SpaceX filing says any Tesla merger needs Musk's approval, even though he has stepped back from the talks
item.description: SpaceX's third-quarter 10-Q lists three approvals for a combination with Tesla: its special committee, its board and its controlling shareholder, Elon Musk. Here is what that means for Tesla shareholders.

item.title: Does a Tesla Powerwall pay off in the Netherlands once net metering ends in 2027?
item.description: Dutch net metering ends on 1 January 2027, and Tesla now sells both the Powerwall 3 and the three-phase Powerwall 3P in the Netherlands. Here is what changes, what a battery can realistically save and when it makes sense.

item.title: Tesla's new Model 3 and Model Y in Japan get vehicle-to-load and a CHAdeMO adapter for 14,000 fast chargers
item.description: Tesla Japan has launched updated Model 3 and Model Y cars that can power appliances, plus a CHAdeMO adapter that unlocks about 14,000 extra fast chargers. A discount worth up to ¥264,000 goes to the first 5,000 buyers.

item.title: Tesla Premium Connectivity vs Standard: what you get, what it costs in the US, UK and Europe, and is it worth it
item.description: Standard Connectivity is free for eight years; Premium costs $9.99, £9.99 or €9.99 a month. What each tier includes, how trials and lifetime Premium work, and when paying makes sense.

item.title: Who will succeed Musk as Tesla CEO? What the board and his pay award say about succession
item.description: Tesla has never named a successor, but Musk must deliver a CEO succession framework to earn the last two tranches of his 2025 award. How Tesla's succession process works, and what the filings allow.

item.title: How much does Starlink cost now? US, UK and German prices after the 2026 increase
item.description: Starlink raised most monthly plans by $5 to $10 in 2026 while hardware got cheaper. Current prices for home and Roam plans, the extra fees, and what it means for Tesla owners using a Starlink Mini.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 vs Model Y in 2026: prices, range, space and which one to buy
item.description: The Model Y costs $1,500 to $3,000 more than the equivalent Model 3 but offers far more cargo space. A side-by-side guide to prices in the US and Europe, range, performance and the cheaper Standard versions.

item.title: Musk's Twitter fraud verdict: November 24 claims deadline, the July ruling, and why Tesla shareholders care
item.description: A jury found two of Musk's 2022 tweets misled Twitter investors, and a judge largely upheld the verdict. Where the case stands, who can claim, and its links to Musk's Tesla share sales.

item.title: Tesla stock ends earnings week up 4.9%: a merger-fuelled rally, then a post-results slide
item.description: Tesla shares closed Friday at $372.22, up 4.9% for the week. Three straight gains ahead of the Q3 report and the SpaceX merger committee news were followed by two down days after the earnings call.

item.title: Tesla cancels the Cybertruck in Australia and New Zealand after seven years of reservations
item.description: Tesla is refunding Cybertruck deposits in Australia and New Zealand and offering a free year of FSD instead. The move suggests a right-hand-drive Cybertruck, including for the UK, is not coming.

item.title: Starlink Mobile passes 22 million users: how VEON and Rogers customers use SpaceX's phone satellites
item.description: SpaceX's direct-to-phone service grew 37% in a quarter, mostly through partner carriers. What VEON's 11 million users and Rogers' expansion show, and what it could mean for connected Teslas.

item.title: Tesla delivery day checklist: what to prepare, what to inspect and what to do if something is wrong
item.description: A practical guide to collecting a new Tesla in the US, UK or Europe: the app steps before the day, an exterior and interior checklist, and how to report problems.

item.title: Musk and the SEC: from 'funding secured' and the 'Twitter sitter' to a $1.5 million Twitter fine
item.description: How Musk's two biggest SEC cases ended, why he is no longer Tesla's chairman, and what the 2026 settlement over his Twitter stake does and does not change for Tesla.

item.title: Tesla's Robotaxi app code hints at letting owners add their own cars to the fleet
item.description: A teardown of Tesla Robotaxi app version 26.10 found code for enrolling privately owned Teslas in the ride-hailing network, chosen by VIN. It also reveals rider features such as AR car finding and rear-seat controls. Nothing is confirmed yet.

item.title: Inside the new Tesla Roadster: a fighter-jet style screen, Track Mode and stunts the car does by itself
item.description: A new Tesla video shows the Roadster's cockpit software, from aero settings to a thruster pressure readout. Musk says owners will be able to let the car perform its stunts autonomously, and promises a looping test track in Texas.

item.title: Tesla Energy's order book: $10.7 billion in contracted revenue and $3.3 billion paid upfront
item.description: Tesla's Q3 2026 filing shows long-term energy contracts worth $10.73 billion still to be delivered, and customer prepayments that jumped by almost $1 billion in three months. Here is what those numbers say about Megapack demand.

item.title: SpaceX eyes 80,000 US cell towers for Starlink Mobile as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile push back at the FCC
item.description: SpaceX is reportedly negotiating access to tens of thousands of cell sites, while the big carriers try to limit new satellite-to-phone rules. What it means for the networks Tesla cars depend on.

item.title: EV incentives for Tesla buyers in 2026: what is left in the US, UK, Germany and the Netherlands
item.description: The US credit is gone and the UK grant excludes Tesla, but Germany now pays up to €6,000 and Dutch tax breaks are shrinking. A country-by-country guide for anyone buying a Tesla in 2026.

item.title: What is Elon Musk's actual job at Tesla? CEO, director and 'Technoking', but not chairman
item.description: Musk is Tesla's CEO and largest shareholder, yet he has not chaired the board since 2018 and takes no salary. What his titles mean, the job conditions in his pay awards, and his many other roles.

item.title: Tesla's $10.1 billion solar factory wins Fort Bend County tax breaks that could last 35 years
item.description: Texas county commissioners voted 4-0 for a 10-year abatement and long rebates for Project Crystal Sun. Tesla still has not picked the site, and the state must sign off.

item.title: Tesla warranty explained: what is covered in the US, UK and Europe, from the battery to used cars
item.description: Four years for the car, eight for the battery, and different mileage limits on each side of the Atlantic. A plain guide to Tesla's warranties, the 70% battery promise, used-car cover and your legal rights in Europe.

item.title: Who sits on Tesla's board in 2026? The nine directors, their ties to Musk and how independent they are
item.description: Tesla's board decides on Elon Musk's pay and the SpaceX merger question. Here is who the nine directors are, which links Tesla considers harmless, and why critics still question the board's independence.

item.title: Tesla maintenance schedule: what servicing your Tesla really needs, and how often
item.description: No oil changes and no mandatory annual service, but tyres, filters, brake fluid and brakes still need attention. Tesla's recommended intervals for Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, in plain language.

item.title: How much does a Tesla Supercharger cost in 2026? US prices by state, and 6 ways to pay less
item.description: Supercharger prices in the US have crept up this year, with big differences between states and between members and non-members. Here is what a charge costs now, and how to keep the bill down.

item.title: Tesla Optimus history: the humanoid robot's road from 2021 reveal to 2026 production
item.description: Five years ago Optimus was an idea on a stage. Now Tesla says it is building production-quality robots in Fremont. A clear timeline of every key step, promise and delay.

item.title: Starlink vs Amazon Leo: where the satellite internet race stands in October 2026
item.description: Starlink has about 11,100 satellites and 13.6 million subscribers. Amazon's Leo has fewer than 400 satellites and has not launched service yet. Here is how the two compare, and why it matters for Tesla.

item.title: Tesla's Megafactories explained: Lathrop, Shanghai and Texas, and their 110 GWh of Megapack capacity
item.description: Tesla now builds its Megapack grid batteries in three dedicated plants on two continents. Here is what each one does, how big they are and why the network matters.

item.title: Tesla Sentry Mode explained: how it works, how much battery it uses, and the privacy rules in Europe
item.description: Sentry Mode turns a parked Tesla into a security camera. Here is how it works, what USB drive you need, how much range it costs per day, and why the rules are stricter in Europe.

item.title: Tesla's deals with Musk's other companies: every related-party transaction in the 2026 proxy
item.description: Megapacks for xAI, Cybertrucks for SpaceX, ads on X and a $2 billion SpaceX stake: Tesla's proxy statement lists what it bought from and sold to companies linked to Elon Musk and its directors.
